subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm critically reviewing the renders against gray wolf identity cues like the lupine head shape and bushy tail, and noticing the body looks too thin with spindly, stick-like front legs that seem disproportionate to the base.

The neck ruff reads as too spiky and dark, more porcupine-like than wolf fur, and should be broadened with fewer, less feathered tufts. The head and ears look mostly fine, but the tail is too short and flat, hanging like a tongue rather than bushy, so it needs more volume and a slight curve, and I'm also noting the banner pole awkwardly obscures the wolf in the three-quarter view.

I'm working out the camera orientation and prop placement — figuring out which side of the model faces the viewer in each shot so I can reposition the banner to clear the wolf's silhouette without overlapping the obelisk or pine props.

I need to reposition the banner away from where it's blocking the view, maybe to the far side near the obelisk, and adjust the pine's placement too so nothing overlaps the wolf head in the final render.

I'm reconsidering the position, trying the right side instead near the rump, checking how the pine and banner pole line up in the three-quarter view so nothing overlaps the wolf's body or flank.

Checking screen positions again, the banner at this placement mostly clears the wolf's body except for slight tail overlap, but it ends up visually colliding with the pine tree in front view since both sit near the same x-range. I should probably shift the pine further back to avoid that overlap.

I'm checking spacing so the pine doesn't collide with the wolf's body or tail, trying positions like (0.6,-0.9) and verifying distances from center stay within the decagon radius without overlapping the tail region near x=0.

Now I'm repositioning the obelisk so it doesn't visually collide with the wolf's head or ears in the three-quarter view, testing coordinates like (-1.0,-0.7) and (-1.0,0.7) and comparing screen-space x ranges against where the head and nose land to keep the obelisk clearly separated to the left.

I'm also adjusting the frost crystals and rocks, which currently sit too close to the obelisk, nudging their base position to roughly (-0.45, 1.0) so they read as a distinct foreground cluster near the wolf's paws in the front view while staying balanced against the banner on the right side.

Finalizing rock positions to avoid overlap with the tail tip and obelisk, then checking snow mound placements against the obelisk's base footprint for clearance.

Looking at proportions from different angles, the legs read too long and narrow and the mane tufts look like spiky armor plates rather than fur — I want to widen and shorten them, reduce their count, and lighten the color with cream roots so they lie flatter along the back instead of standing up like shingles.

The neck ruff looks too spiky, like a big bib, so I want to reduce the tuft count and lengths while making them wider and overlapping for softer contrast—dropping the first ring from 12 to 10 items and shortening/widening them, same for the second ring.

Now I'm thinking about the body: the chest needs more volume since wolves have deep but narrow chests, and currently the front legs look too narrow and straight at the shoulders.

I want to thicken the legs and enlarge the paws, and adjust the tail to be bushier and curve outward so it's visible from the back view instead of dropping straight down—extending its path and widening its radii along the length. I also notice the hind legs look too spindly from the back, with a narrow hip/thigh area that needs more mass.

The war-paint marks on the head look like a weird dotted checker pattern rather than a clean slash—likely caused by low texel density on the texture sheet for such a small head area. I should replace it with a smoother diagonal band using something like smoothstep instead of the current sparse pattern causing the stipple effect.

Rather than doubling the texture resolution and risking atlas overflow, I'll just thicken the stripes instead—widening the stripe width relative to the period so each chevron spans more texels, giving a bolder, cleaner war paint look across the cheek. The leg bands are already a reasonable width, so I'll leave those as is.

The paint sheet's density gets diluted by large flat areas like the base, so I should paint those with solid flat colors (snow a pale blue-white, stone with subtle variation) to balance things out. I'll go with paintSize 2048 and a 4096 atlas, packing the rune ring at 512 and other textures at 256 so everything fits. I also want to enlarge the eye decals slightly so they're more visible from the front, and I'm noting the jaw's lower lip needs a closer look since it's a separate cream-colored piece.

I'm now spotting a stray chin tuft hanging below the jaw that looks like an odd hook-shaped extrusion — that needs to be removed or replaced. The neck collar strap looks fine even though partially hidden, and there's no visible fang pendant to worry about. I'm also noticing stray tan tuft bars sticking out near the ears that should be removed, and I'm considering thinning out the dorsal mane spikes along the spine, keeping only the central and side rows with a lighter color.

I'm limiting side tufts to appear only further down the neck region, reducing the dark fur card counts on the neck and body, and lightening their colors so the back doesn't look so spiky and dark. The chest coloring and ear tuft function placement both look fine as they are.

I'm debating whether to shrink the base radius to make the wolf fill the frame better, but that would ripple through too many coordinates, so I'll leave the body scale alone and just keep the rune ring size as is. I'm also checking whether moving the obelisk further out would push its corners past the frame edge.

I'm checking whether shifting the obelisk's screen position avoids overlap with the wolf head's nose and muzzle, testing a few coordinate tweaks and finding the body width still collides with the nose region.

I'll settle on obelisk position (-0.95, 0.6) with a slightly smaller plinth to clear the nose, updating the OX and OZ variables in the obelisk code accordingly.

Checking the wolf position at x=0, I'm moving the crystals base from (-0.72,0.95) to roughly (0.45,1.0) to avoid conflicts, keeping them clear of the banner and paws in the front view. I'm also nudging the mound from (0.85,0.85) toward (0.95,0.8) to keep it separated from the crystal cluster's radius.

Still adjusting rock and crystal positions to avoid overlaps...

Finalizing the rock and mound positions, checking each against nearby elements like the hind leg to avoid overlap, settling on four rocks plus the mound placement.

I'm adjusting the crystal cluster's base coordinates, moving it slightly and checking the pine tree and banner placement for clearance against the wolf figure so nothing overlaps in the front view. I'm deciding to skip rescaling the wolf base for now and move on to checking the loose octahedron element.

Now I'm preparing the actual edit list: increasing the paint resolution in the builder config, updating the grey and cream mane color blends to use a cooler steel-blue palette, and adjusting the war paint pattern on the head by tweaking the stripe frequency formula.

Then I'm moving on to updating the tuft SVG colors to match the new cooler palette, and reworking the tail's spine curve control points and radii profile for a more tapered, natural shape.

Next I'm increasing the leg radii slightly for thicker limbs, enlarging the eye size for proportion, removing the chin tuft geometry entirely, and continuing into the ear tuft placement loop.

Adjusting ear tuft positions, then rewriting the dorsal mane loop to use a shorter base length with a width bump and limiting side tufts to only the later segments (i>=4) for a cleaner taper, before moving on to the neck ring details.

Checking the plinth's corner overhang against the apothem distance, I realize it's already slightly overhanging, so I'm shrinking the plinth box size down to tighten it up.

Still adjusting coordinates...

Making sure the ring call with unique counts and radii stays distinct to avoid search ambiguity.
